''See also: [[World Spirit Timeline]]''

== Overview ==
{{spoiler|book=lh-04-the-pilot|A World Spirit is a non-biological manifestation of [[Aether]] that represents a fundamental concept or celestial body. Rather than being physical beings, they function similarly to digital avatars; while they can project themselves into reality in various forms—ranging from human-like figures to massive entities made of stone, soil, or smoke—their true existence remains beyond mortal influence. These spirits are intrinsically linked to the Aetheric identity of the locations they represent, such as planets, moons, or even ships. For example, a ship's World Spirit can be bound to the vessel, while planetary spirits may possess consciousness spread across an entire world. [[World Spirits]] play a vital role in maintaining planetary habitability and protecting ecosystems through their influence over [[Aether flows]]. They possess immense power, capable of generating massive storms, lightning blasts, or protective shields, and in some cases, their influence is so vast they can protect entire star systems. Because of this connection, the death of a World Spirit can lead to the rapid collapse of a planet's environment. While they are powerful, they are often bound by their fundamental nature and can be summoned through specific rituals, though catching their attention is difficult as they often perceive mortal life as insignificant. They can also be studied in their nascent stages or even consumed.}}

== The Knight ==
{{spoiler|book=lh-03-the-knight|[[World Spirits]] are entities capable of being engaged in bargains. While [[Beshkin]] possesses a World Spirit noted for its neutrality, the moon of [[Titan Force headquarters]] lacks one of its own. The narrator utilizes a World Spirit to assist with the process of casting. During a confrontation, this spirit defends against [[Neth’terith]] by deploying green shields and discharging lightning blasts.}}

<div class="wv-facts mw-collapsible mw-collapsed"><div class="wv-facts-head mw-collapsible-toggle">Sourced facts <span class="wv-facts-count">5</span></div>
<ul class="wv-fact-list mw-collapsible-content">
<li>{{spoiler|book=lh-03-the-knight|[[World Spirits]] are entities that can be bargained with.<ref name="lh-03-the-knight-c11">''The Knight'', chapter 11</ref>}}</li>
<li>{{spoiler|book=lh-03-the-knight|The narrator has a [[World Spirit]] to help with casting.<ref name="lh-03-the-knight-c18">''The Knight'', chapter 18</ref>}}</li>
<li>{{spoiler|book=lh-03-the-knight|The [[World Spirit]] resists [[Neth’terith]] with lightning blasts and green shields.<ref name="lh-03-the-knight-c20">''The Knight'', chapter 20</ref>}}</li>
<li>{{spoiler|book=lh-03-the-knight|[[Beshkin]] has a [[World Spirit]] known for its neutrality.<ref name="lh-03-the-knight-c21">''The Knight'', chapter 21</ref>}}</li>
<li>{{spoiler|book=lh-03-the-knight|The moon of [[Titan Force headquarters]] does not have its own [[World Spirit]].<ref name="lh-03-the-knight-c38">''The Knight'', chapter 38</ref>}}</li>
</ul></div>

== The Pilot ==
{{spoiler|book=lh-04-the-pilot|One of approximately a million spirits existing across various planets, the World Spirit possesses a chaotic and unreliable nature. Driven by an eagerness to alter the development of [[Basyrryx]], this entity has the ability to manifest itself to provide information. During a pivotal moment, it clasped hands with the narrator to finalize a deal. However, this interaction led to the narrator casting a sealing spell against the spirit, marking the first time the narrator had ever cursed such an entity.}}
